definitions.explanation: Food served quickly and cheaply over a counter — hamburgers, gyudon, fried chicken and the like — and by extension the restaurants that serve it. From English "fast food".

examples.japanese: {昼|ひる}はファストフードで{済|す}ませた。
examples.english: I made do with fast food for lunch.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}にファストフードの{店|みせ}が{三軒|さんげん}ある。
examples.english: There are three fast-food places in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しい{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}くと、どうしてもファストフードに{頼|たよ}りがちになってしまう。
examples.english: When busy days continue, I inevitably end up relying on fast food.

notes:
Both ファストフード and ファーストフード are current; ファストフード is the form preferred by newspapers and industry bodies, while ファーストフード remains common in speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ファストフード{店|てん}: a fast-food restaurant
- ファストフードで{済|す}ませる: to make do with fast food
- ファストフード{業界|ぎょうかい}: the fast-food industry

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {外食|がいしょく}: eating out — any restaurant meal, with no implication of speed or cheapness
- {軽食|けいしょく}: a light meal, snack — describes portion size rather than the style of service
